Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১) Which is not an anxiety disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Depressive disorder is not an anxiety disorder. It is a mood (affective) disorder characterized by persistent sadness, loss of interest, low energy, sleep and appetite changes, and impaired concentration.

The other options are types of anxiety disorders:

  • Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD): Excessive and persistent worry about multiple areas of life.

  • Panic disorder: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with intense fear and autonomic symptoms.

  • Phobic anxiety disorder: Excessive fear and avoidance of specific objects or situations.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anxiety disorders:

    • Generalized anxiety disorder

    • Panic disorder

    • Phobic disorders

    • Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

    • Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)

  • Depressive disorder → Mood disorder

Exam Pearl:
Depression is a mood disorder, not an anxiety disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ২) What is a major cause of disability & suicide?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Depression is a major cause of disability and suicide worldwide. Major depressive disorder can cause persistent low mood, loss of interest, hopelessness, impaired functioning, and suicidal thoughts or attempts. It is one of the leading contributors to global disease burden.

The other options:

  • Mania: A feature of bipolar disorder characterized by elevated mood, increased energy, and impulsive behavior; suicide risk may occur in bipolar disorder but mania itself is not the major cause of disability.

  • Dysthymia (Persistent depressive disorder): A chronic but usually milder depressive condition.

  • OCD: Causes significant disability but is not the leading cause of suicide compared with major depression.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major depressive disorder:

    • ↓ Mood

    • ↓ Interest/pleasure (anhedonia)

    • Sleep/appetite disturbance

    • Suicidal ideation

  • Depression = major cause of disability + suicide risk

Exam Pearl:
Depression is the most important psychiatric disorder associated with disability and suicide.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৩) Which is also referred to as neurasthenia?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) is also referred to as neurasthenia in older psychiatric terminology. It is characterized by persistent and unexplained fatigue, weakness, reduced concentration, sleep disturbance, and worsening symptoms after physical or mental exertion.

The other options:

  • Somatization disorder: Multiple physical symptoms without adequate medical explanation, associated with psychological factors.

  • Conversion disorder: Neurological symptoms (e.g., paralysis, blindness, seizures) due to psychological conflict without organic disease.

  • Hypochondriacal disorder: Excessive fear or belief of having a serious illness despite medical reassurance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Neurasthenia = Chronic fatigue syndrome

  • Features:

    • Persistent fatigue

    • Easy fatigability

    • Poor concentration

    • Sleep disturbance

  • Somatization: Multiple unexplained physical complaints

  • Conversion: Psychological conflict → neurological symptoms

Exam Pearl:
Neurasthenia is an older term associated with chronic fatigue syndrome.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৪) Patient with anxiety often also have......?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Patients with anxiety disorders often have comorbid depression. Anxiety and depressive disorders frequently occur together because they share common biological, psychological, and environmental risk factors. The presence of both conditions can increase symptom severity and functional impairment.

The other options:

  • Conversion disorder: May occur with psychological stress but is not the most common comorbidity with anxiety disorders.

  • Stress disorder: Some anxiety disorders are stress-related (e.g., PTSD), but it is not the typical associated condition asked here.

  • Eating disorder: Can coexist with anxiety, but less commonly than depression.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Common psychiatric comorbidity of anxiety disorders:

    • Depression (most common)

    • Substance use disorders

    • Other anxiety disorders

  • Anxiety + depression → increased risk of disability and suicide.

Exam Pearl:
Anxiety disorders commonly coexist with depression.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৫) Which group of drug is not used as antidepressants?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Benzodiazepines (BDZs) are not used as antidepressants. They are primarily used as anxiolytics, sedatives, hypnotics, anticonvulsants, and muscle relaxants. They may reduce anxiety symptoms but do not treat the underlying depression.

The other options are classes of antidepressant drugs:

  • TCAs (Tricyclic antidepressants): e.g., amitriptyline, imipramine.

  • MAOIs (Monoamine oxidase inhibitors): e.g., phenelzine, tranylcypromine.

  • SSRIs (Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors): e.g., fluoxetine, sertraline.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major antidepressant groups:

    • SSRIs (first-line commonly)

    • SNRIs

    • TCAs

    • MAOIs

    • Atypical antidepressants

  • Benzodiazepines:

    • ↑ GABA-A activity

    • Used for anxiety and insomnia

    • Risk: tolerance and dependence

Exam Pearl:
BDZs treat anxiety, not depression; TCAs, MAOIs, and SSRIs are antidepressant classes.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৬) Loss or distortion of neurological functions that is not fully explained by organic disease is called......?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Conversion disorder is characterized by loss or distortion of neurological functions (such as paralysis, blindness, seizures, sensory loss, or abnormal movements) that cannot be fully explained by an organic neurological disease. These symptoms are believed to be related to psychological factors.

The other options:

  • Somatization disorder: Multiple physical symptoms affecting different systems without adequate medical explanation.

  • Chronic fatigue syndrome: Persistent unexplained fatigue with associated symptoms.

  • Hypochondriacal disorder: Excessive preoccupation or fear of having a serious illness despite medical reassurance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Conversion disorder:

    • Neurological symptoms without organic cause

    • Associated with psychological stress/conflict

    • Common symptoms:

      • Paralysis

      • Blindness

      • Non-epileptic seizures

      • Sensory loss

  • Somatization → Multiple unexplained physical complaints

Exam Pearl:
Unexplained neurological deficit due to psychological factors = Conversion disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৭) 'Excessive fear of dying in an air crush leading to avoidance of flying' - is......?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Phobic disorder is characterized by an excessive, irrational, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, leading to avoidance behavior. Fear of dying in an airplane crash and avoiding flying is an example of specific phobia (situational type).

The other options:

  • Panic disorder: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks, not necessarily triggered by a specific situation.

  • OCD (Obsessive-compulsive disorder): Characterized by intrusive thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors (compulsions).

  • Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD): Excessive anxiety and worry about multiple areas of life for a prolonged period.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Specific phobia: Fear of a particular object/situation

    • Flying

    • Heights

    • Animals

    • Injections

  • Panic disorder: Sudden episodes of intense fear + autonomic symptoms

  • GAD: Excessive worry about many things

Exam Pearl:
Fear of flying with avoidance = specific phobic disorder (situational phobia).

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৮) A 20 years old female presented with loss of interest in activity, decreased appetite, early morning awakening. what is most probable diagnosis?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
The most probable diagnosis is depression (Major Depressive Disorder). The key features are:

  • Loss of interest in activities (anhedonia)

  • Decreased appetite

  • Early morning awakening (a typical biological symptom of depression)

These are classic symptoms of a depressive episode, especially the early morning awakening, which is a characteristic sleep disturbance in melancholic depression.

The other options:

  • Conversion disorder: Presents with neurological symptoms (e.g., paralysis, blindness) without organic cause.

  • Stress disorder: Usually related to a specific traumatic or stressful event.

  • Anxiety disorder: Characterized mainly by excessive fear, worry, and autonomic symptoms.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major depression symptoms (SIGECAPS):

    • Sleep disturbance (early morning awakening)

    • Interest decreased (anhedonia)

    • Guilt/worthlessness

    • Energy decreased

    • Concentration impaired

    • Appetite change

    • Psychomotor change

    • Suicidal thoughts

Exam Pearl:
Anhedonia + decreased appetite + early morning awakening = Major depressive disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ৯) Which is a disadvantage of using SSRIs over TCAs?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
A disadvantage of SSRIs (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors) compared with TCAs (Tricyclic Antidepressants) is that SSRIs commonly cause sexual dysfunction, including:

  • Decreased libido

  • Delayed ejaculation

  • Anorgasmia

This occurs due to increased serotonin activity inhibiting sexual function pathways.

The other options:

  • Less bioavailability: Not a major disadvantage of SSRIs; many SSRIs have good oral bioavailability.

  • Short half-life: Some SSRIs have short half-lives, but this is not the key disadvantage compared with TCAs.

  • Causes muscarinic & adrenergic adverse effects: This is a disadvantage of TCAs, not SSRIs. TCAs cause anticholinergic effects, sedation, and postural hypotension.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Drug class Important adverse effects
SSRIs Sexual dysfunction, GI upset, serotonin syndrome
TCAs Anticholinergic effects, cardiac toxicity, sedation
MAOIs Hypertensive crisis with tyramine-containing foods

Exam Pearl:
SSRIs are safer than TCAs but commonly cause sexual side effects (↓ libido, anorgasmia).

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১০) Patients with which disorder make inappropriate request for cosmetic surgery?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) is characterized by excessive preoccupation with an imagined or minor defect in physical appearance. Patients often believe they have a significant cosmetic flaw and may make repeated or inappropriate requests for cosmetic surgery to correct it.

The other options:

  • Somatization disorder: Multiple unexplained physical symptoms involving different body systems.

  • Conversion disorder: Neurological symptoms without organic disease due to psychological factors.

  • Hypochondriacal disorder (Illness anxiety disorder): Excessive fear or belief of having a serious disease despite medical reassurance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Body dysmorphic disorder:

    • Preoccupation with appearance defect

    • Repeated mirror checking

    • Seeking cosmetic procedures

    • Commonly associated with depression and anxiety

  • Hypochondriasis: Fear of illness, not appearance defect

Exam Pearl:
Unreasonable demand for cosmetic surgery due to perceived body defect = Body dysmorphic disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১১) Which is associated somatic symptom of generalized anxiety disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Palpitations are a classic somatic symptom of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) due to increased sympathetic nervous system activity. Patients with GAD commonly experience autonomic symptoms such as increased heart rate, sweating, trembling, and muscle tension.

The other options:

  • Bowel disturbance: May occur in anxiety, but is less characteristic as a classic somatic symptom.

  • Chest pain: Can occur during anxiety or panic attacks, but is not the typical GAD symptom asked here.

  • Paresthesia: More commonly associated with panic attacks due to hyperventilation-induced changes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:
GAD symptoms:

  • Excessive worry (>6 months)

  • Restlessness

  • Fatigue

  • Poor concentration

  • Irritability

  • Muscle tension

  • Sleep disturbance

  • Autonomic symptoms:

    • Palpitations

    • Sweating

    • Trembling

Exam Pearl:
GAD commonly presents with autonomic symptoms, especially palpitations due to sympathetic overactivity.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১২) Which somatoform disorder is also known as health anxiety?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Hypochondriacal disorder (Illness anxiety disorder) is a somatoform disorder characterized by excessive preoccupation with having a serious illness despite medical reassurance. It is also known as health anxiety because patients have persistent fear and belief that they are suffering from a disease.

The other options:

  • Somatization disorder: Multiple physical symptoms affecting different organ systems without adequate medical explanation.

  • Conversion disorder: Loss or disturbance of neurological function without organic disease.

  • Chronic fatigue syndrome: Persistent unexplained fatigue, historically related to neurasthenia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypochondriasis = Health anxiety

    • Fear of serious illness

    • Repeated checking and medical consultations

    • Misinterpretation of normal bodily sensations

  • Somatization → Multiple physical complaints

  • Conversion → Neurological symptoms without organic cause

Exam Pearl:
Health anxiety (excessive fear of illness) = Hypochondriacal disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৩) All of the following are features of generalized anxiety disorder except........ ?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent and excessive anxiety and worry about multiple areas of life, usually occurring for at least 6 months. Symptoms are not limited to exposure to a specific trigger.

Features of GAD include:

  • Persistent occurrence

  • Excessive worry

  • Agitation/restlessness

  • Muscle tension, fatigue, poor concentration, sleep disturbance

Symptoms on exposure are more typical of phobic anxiety disorders, where anxiety occurs when the person is exposed to a specific feared object or situation.

The other options:

  • Persistent occurrence: True for GAD.

  • Agitation: Common feature of GAD.

  • Worry: Core symptom of GAD.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • GAD: Free-floating anxiety + excessive worry (not linked to a specific stimulus)

  • Phobia: Anxiety occurs on exposure to a specific trigger

  • Panic disorder: Sudden unexpected panic attacks

Exam Pearl:
GAD = persistent worry without specific exposure trigger; exposure-related symptoms suggest phobia.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৪) Which is not a treatment option for anxiety disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Total avoidance of a feared situation is not a treatment option for anxiety disorders. Avoidance may temporarily reduce anxiety, but it reinforces the fear and can worsen the disorder over time. Effective treatment usually involves gradual exposure rather than complete avoidance.

The other options:

  • Relaxation techniques: Help reduce anxiety symptoms.

  • Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT): A first-line psychological treatment for many anxiety disorders.

  • Antidepressants: SSRIs and SNRIs are commonly used pharmacological treatments.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anxiety disorder treatment:

    • CBT (especially exposure-based therapy)

    • Relaxation techniques

    • SSRIs/SNRIs

    • Anxiolytics in selected cases

  • Avoidance behavior → maintains anxiety

Exam Pearl:
Anxiety is treated by controlled exposure, not total avoidance of feared situations.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৫) Which is not a somatoform disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Anorexia nervosa is not a somatoform disorder; it is classified as an eating disorder characterized by:

  • Restriction of food intake

  • Intense fear of gaining weight

  • Distorted body image

  • Low body weight

The other options are somatoform disorders:

  • Conversion disorder: Neurological symptoms without an identifiable organic cause.

  • Pain disorder: Persistent pain influenced by psychological factors.

  • Hypochondriasis (Illness anxiety disorder): Excessive fear or belief of having a serious illness.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Somatoform disorders:

    • Somatization disorder

    • Conversion disorder

    • Pain disorder

    • Hypochondriasis

    • Body dysmorphic disorder

  • Eating disorders:

    • Anorexia nervosa

    • Bulimia nervosa

Exam Pearl:
Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder, not a somatoform disorder.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৬) Chronic low grade depressed mood without sufficient other symptoms is called.....?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Dysthymia (Persistent Depressive Disorder) is characterized by a chronic low-grade depressed mood that persists for a long period but does not meet the full criteria for major depressive disorder due to insufficient additional symptoms.

The other options:

  • Unipolar depression: Major depressive disorder with a more severe depressive episode and multiple symptoms.

  • Mania: A state of elevated mood, increased energy, and impulsive behavior.

  • Bipolar disorder: Characterized by episodes of both depression and mania/hypomania.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Dysthymia:

    • Chronic depressed mood (≥2 years in adults)

    • Mild severity

    • Fewer symptoms than major depression

  • Major depression: More severe symptoms with functional impairment

  • Bipolar disorder: Depression + mania

Exam Pearl:
Chronic low-grade depression without sufficient symptoms for major depression = Dysthymia.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৭) What is true about somatization disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Somatization disorder is more common in females. It is characterized by multiple unexplained physical symptoms involving different organ systems, often beginning before the age of 30 and associated with psychological distress.

The other options:

  • More in male: Incorrect; prevalence is higher in females.

  • Same in both male & female: Incorrect; there is a clear female predominance.

  • No relation with sex: Incorrect.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Somatization disorder:

    • More common in female

    • Multiple medically unexplained symptoms

    • Often associated with anxiety and depression

    • Chronic course

  • Conversion disorder: Also more common in females.

Exam Pearl:
Somatoform disorders, especially somatization disorder, show a female predominance.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৮) 'Repeated hand-washing related to thoughts of contamination ' - what type of psychiatric disorder is meant here?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Repeated hand-washing due to thoughts of contamination is a classic feature of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD).

  • Obsessions: Recurrent, intrusive thoughts (e.g., fear of contamination or germs).

  • Compulsions: Repetitive behaviors performed to reduce anxiety caused by obsessions (e.g., excessive hand-washing).

The other options:

  • Phobia: Irrational fear of a specific object or situation with avoidance behavior.

  • Panic: Sudden episodes of intense fear with autonomic symptoms.

  • HCR (Hypochondriacal disorder): Excessive fear or belief of having a serious illness.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • OCD = Obsession + Compulsion

    • Contamination fear → excessive washing

    • Doubt → repeated checking

    • Intrusive thoughts → repetitive rituals

Exam Pearl:
Contamination thoughts with repeated hand-washing = OCD.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ১৯) Which is not true about conversion disorder?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
In conversion disorder, neurological symptoms occur without an identifiable organic lesion. Hoover sign is usually present (positive) in functional limb weakness and helps differentiate it from true neurological weakness. Therefore, saying “Hoover sign absent” is not true.

The other options:

  • Plantar flexor: Can be seen in conversion disorder because there is no true upper motor neuron lesion.

  • Normal jerks: Reflexes are usually normal in conversion disorder.

  • Spasticity absent: True; spasticity suggests an organic upper motor neuron lesion, not conversion disorder.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Conversion disorder features:

    • Inconsistent neurological signs

    • Normal reflexes

    • No muscle wasting

    • No spasticity

    • Positive Hoover sign in functional weakness

    • Symptoms often related to psychological stress

Exam Pearl:
Conversion disorder → positive Hoover sign; absent Hoover sign is not typical.

Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.question: ২০) Which is a newer antidepressants?
Anxiety neurosis, Depression, Dissociati.exp:
Escitalopram is a newer antidepressant belonging to the Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI) class. SSRIs are newer-generation antidepressants and are commonly used as first-line treatment for depression due to better safety and tolerability.

The other options:

  • Amitriptyline: A tricyclic antidepressant (TCA); older antidepressant.

  • Phenelzine: A monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI); older antidepressant.

  • Mirtazapine: A newer atypical antidepressant, but among the given options, escitalopram is the classic SSRI newer antidepressant.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Newer antidepressants:

    • SSRIs → Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Escitalopram

    • SNRIs → Venlafaxine, Duloxetine

    • Atypical → Mirtazapine, Bupropion

  • Older antidepressants:

    • TCAs → Amitriptyline, Imipramine

    • MAOIs → Phenelzine

Exam Pearl:
Escitalopram is a newer-generation SSRI antidepressant and commonly used first-line.
